topic.title: Sarnath: India's 45th UNESCO World Heritage Site

subtopics.title: Inscription and India's World Heritage status
subtopics.summary: Sarnath was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List at the 48th session of the World Heritage Committee, held in Busan, Republic of Korea. With this inscription India has 45 World Heritage Sites, ranking 6th globally and 2nd in the Asia-Pacific region. Of these sites, 37 are cultural, 7 are natural and 1 is mixed.
facts: Inscribed during the 48th session of the World Heritage Committee in Busan (Republic of Korea)
With Sarnath, India now has 45 UNESCO World Heritage Sites
India ranks 6th globally and 2nd in the Asia-Pacific region
India's sites: 37 Cultural, 7 Natural, 1 Mixed
Khangchendzonga National Park (Sikkim) is India's mixed heritage site

Dholavira (Gujarat) is the only Indus Valley Civilization site from India on the list
India hosted the 46th Annual Session at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi
India served as a Committee Member for the 2021-2025 term

subtopics.title: Sarnath's sites and the first sermon
subtopics.summary: Sarnath is where Gautama Buddha gave his first sermon after attaining enlightenment at Bodhgaya, an event known as Dharmachakra Pravartana. The site has ancient names including Rishipatana, Ishipatana and Mrigadava. Its archaeological features include several stupas, a vihara and the Ashokan Pillar, each associated with a particular event or ruler.
facts: Ancient names: Rishipatana, Ishipatana and Mrigadava (Deer Park)
Buddha gave his first sermon at Sarnath after enlightenment at Bodhgaya
The first sermon is known as Dharmachakra Pravartana (Turning of the Wheel of the Law)
The sermon marks the beginning of the Buddhist Sangha
Chaukhandi Stupa: meeting of Buddha and his first five disciples
Dhamekh Stupa: marks the site of Buddha's first sermon
Dharmarajika Stupa: traditionally associated with Emperor Ashoka and Buddha's relics
Mulagandhakuti Vihara: Buddha's rainy-season retreat at Sarnath
Ashokan Pillar: erected during Ashoka's reign; its Lion Capital is India's National Emblem
Sarnath is one of 4 principal Buddhist pilgrimage sites (with Lumbini, Bodhgaya, Kushinagar)

subtopics.title: UNESCO, the Convention and the recognition process
subtopics.summary: The World Heritage List is maintained by the World Heritage Programme and administered by the UNESCO World Heritage Committee. The Convention concerning Protection of World Cultural and Natural Heritage was adopted in 1972, took effect in 1975, and was ratified by India in 1977. In India the Archaeological Survey of India is the nodal agency, while ICOMOS and IUCN carry out the assessment before the Committee takes the final decision.
facts: UNESCO was founded in 1945; its headquarters are in Paris, France
UNESCO stands for United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization
The World Heritage List is maintained by the World Heritage Programme
The list is administered by the UNESCO World Heritage Committee

India ratified the Convention in 1977

Assessment is done by ICOMOS and IUCN; final decision by the World Heritage Committee

subtopics.title: Gautama Buddha and Buddhism
subtopics.summary: Gautama Buddha was born as Siddhartha in 563 BC at Lumbini, near Kapilavastu, and died at Kushinagara in 487 BC. He taught the Middle Path, the Four Noble Truths and the 8-Fold Path, and he called himself Tathagata. After his death his teachings were divided into three Pitakas at the First Buddhist Council.
facts: Born as Siddhartha in 563 BC at Lumbini (Nepal), near Kapilavastu
Father was an elected ruler of Kapilvastu and headed the Shakya republican clan
Mother was a princess from the Koshalan dynasty
Death (Mahaparinirvana) at Kushinagara in 487 BC

Middle Path (Madhyam Marg): avoid the extremes
Four Noble Truths: suffering, its cause, its ending, and the path to ending it
8-Fold Path: right view, intention, speech, action, livelihood, mindfulness, effort, concentration

quizzes.title: Sarnath: inscription, sites and sermon
quizzes.passage: Sarnath, a Buddhist site in Uttar Pradesh, has recently been inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List. The inscription was made at a meeting of the World Heritage Committee, and it raised the total number of such sites in India. Sarnath holds a special place in Buddhist history because Gautama Buddha gave his first teaching there after attaining enlightenment at Bodhgaya. The event marks the beginning of the Buddhist monastic community, known as the Sangha, and it is linked with the Noble Eightfold Path. The site was known in earlier times by several names, and it is visited today for its monuments. Visitors see the Chaukhandi, Dhamekh and Dharmarajika stupas, a vihara and the Ashokan Pillar. Many of these structures are linked with episodes from the Buddha's life or with rulers of the past. Sarnath is also counted among the principal Buddhist pilgrimage sites, which draw devotees from many countries. India has many heritage sites of different kinds, grouped as cultural, natural and mixed. Each category holds its own set of monuments, and together they show how varied the country's heritage is. The process of recognition involves assessment by expert bodies before the final decision is taken by the committee. Such a listing is a major achievement for any country, because it brings the monument to the attention of the whole world.

III. Dharmarajika Stupa   ->   C. Buddha's first sermon

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Sarnath:
I. Sarnath is one of the four principal Buddhist pilgrimage sites.
II. The Chaukhandi Stupa marks the site of Buddha's first sermon.
III. The Dharmarajika Stupa is traditionally associated with Emperor Ashoka and Buddha's relics.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement II is wrong because the Dhamekh Stupa, not the Chaukhandi Stupa, marks the site of the first sermon.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. Dholavira is the only Indus Valley Civilization site from India on the World Heritage List.
II. Khangchendzonga National Park is India's mixed heritage site.
III. The Mulagandhakuti Vihara marks the site of Buddha's first sermon.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are correct, while statement III is wrong because the Dhamekh Stupa marks the first sermon site.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an ancient name for Sarnath?
questions.explanation: Kushinagar is the place where Buddha died, not an ancient name of Sarnath.

quizzes.title: Buddha's life and Buddhist teachings
quizzes.passage: Gautama Buddha was born as Siddhartha in a noble family near Kapilavastu, close to Lumbini in present-day Nepal. His father was an elected ruler, and his mother came from a royal dynasty of Kosala. Siddhartha left his home in a famous departure and later attained enlightenment, after which people began to call him the Buddha. He spent the rest of his life teaching, and his first sermon was delivered at Sarnath. Buddhism, which developed on the basis of his teachings in the sixth century BC, emphasises the attainment of enlightenment and recommends following a middle path between extremes. Its followers reject the authority of the Vedas and the idea of a permanent soul, which sets Buddhism apart from some other traditions. After the Buddha passed away, his teachings were recited and organised at a series of gatherings known as councils. The first council grouped the teachings into collections, which were later written down. Buddhist texts preserve these teachings in several collections, including the main discourses and the rules of conduct for monks and nuns. The core of his message concerns suffering, its causes, its ending and the path that leads to that ending, and this remains central to the faith. Each of these ideas connects with the others, and together they form the basis of the religion.

questions.q: Which Noble Truth states that suffering could be ended? (one word)
